abstract_sentences_with_numbers: Experiments on CICIoT2023 and UNSW-NB15 show competitive intrusion-detection performance together with improved communication reliability.
On CICIoT2023, the framework reduces end-to-end delay by 26.6\%, increases packet delivery ratio by 13.4\%, improves path stability by 62.8\%, and increases transfer efficiency by 46.0\%.
On UNSW-NB15, the Proposed $\varepsilon\approx20$ configuration improves F1-score by 8.3\% and ROC-AUC by 6.6\% over FedAvg, while reducing delay by 24.7\% and improving path stability by 63.5\%.
It also reduces the noise-to-signal ratio by up to 69.7\% relative to DP+FedAvg.
conclusion_sentences_with_numbers: Experiments on CICIoT2023 and UNSW-NB15 show that the proposed framework maintains competitive intrusion-detection performance while substantially improving network-level behavior.

On CICIoT2023, it reduces end-to-end delay by approximately \(26.6\%\), increases PDR by \(13.4\%\), improves path stability by \(62.8\%\), and increases transfer efficiency by \(46.0\%\) compared with FedAvg.
On UNSW-NB15, Proposed \(\varepsilon\approx20\) improves F1-score by approximately \(8.3\%\) and ROC-AUC by \(6.6\%\), while reducing delay by \(24.7\%\) and improving path stability by \(63.5\%\).

The current study is limited by the trusted or semi-trusted server assumption underlying the server-side Gaussian privacy mechanism, the row-level CICIoT2023 split, and the use of a simulated Edge--Cloud environment.
